title: cross-team-engineering-leadership-weekly-staff-notes-2026-05-18
content:
Attendees: Asha (chair), Miguel, Priya, Evan, Laura, Sam (infra), Noor (platform), Ravi (release), Hannah (product-hosted-api), guests: Kevin (SRE)

Agenda:
- Quick cross-team status updates (5 min each)
- Canary rollout policy and rollback automation
- Recent perf regression investigation + mitigation
- Dedicated capacity autoscaling tuning
- Incident follow-up (PD INC on 5/12)
- Action items and risks for next two sprints

Notes / Updates:
1) Serving Runtime (Asha / Miguel)
- Canary rollout: initial canary for v1.12 kernel selection shipped Monday. Early metrics look OK for 95th latency on small-batch text-gen (<= 10ms regression on some Llama-variant configs). We observed higher token mem usage in 8-bit quantized path for long-context sessions.
- Next step: run extended 24h soak with production traffic split 1% -> 5% -> 10%. Miguel to add extra telemetry for KV cache hit ratio and per-model quantization path.
- PR #1287 contains a mitigation that pins a slower kernel for sequences > 2048 until we finish memory safety checks.

2) Infrastructure / Autoscaling (Sam)
- Autoscaler tuning: recent Dedicated pools experienced slow ramp during the morning spike (5/14). Root cause: pod eviction + node provisioning time in the cloud provider. Sam proposed conservative pre-warm buffer based on rolling 7-day peak; will surface estimated cost delta.
- Action: implement pre-warm policy toggle for Dedicated customers (configurable by tier). Sam to run cost simulation and share numbers by 5/22.

3) Platform & Routing (Noor)
- Smart routing experiment: routing low-priority requests to quantized model variants is showing 18% avg cost savings without visible quality loss in our current eval set. Need expanded A/B on more customer prompts.
- Concern: latency tail for cold-start quantized variant is higher; Noor to add a small warm cache for quantized endpoints.

4) Release Engineering (Ravi)
- Release window for 1.12 scheduled for 5/25. Must freeze non-critical changes by 5/20. Ravi flagged two open PRs that need test infra updates; owners notified.

5) Product / Hosted API (Hannah)
- Feature: per-route token budget exposure in Console beta. Early customers gave positive feedback. Plan to roll to more accounts next quarter.
- Observability ask: product needs clearer token-level labeling in traces to attribute costs to routes. Evan to propose trace labeling convention by 5/21.

Incident Review (PagerDuty INC on 2026-05-12):
- Summary: A misconfigured autoscaling policy caused Dedicated pool to drop below reserved min during a control-plane maintenance window, resulting in 3 degraded customer queries (90-120s timeouts) for ~18 minutes.
- Postmortem notes: change window overlapped with cloud provider maintenance; guardrail missing to prevent scale-down during critical windows.
- Actions:
  - Sam: implement scale-down hold during known provider maintenance windows (5/26 deliverable)
  - Ravi + Noor: add alert when pool capacity drops below reserve for >5m (done: alert ticket created)
  - Ops: update runbook and notify affected customers with postmortem (Asha to review draft)

Performance Regression (5/11-5/14):
- Root cause: new kernel selection heuristics favored a throughput-optimized kernel that regresses small-batch latency for certain attention configs.
- Mitigation: revert heuristic for the affected model types; deploy patch in canary. Miguel to drive deeper profiling and produce a follow-up optimization plan.

Decisions made:
- Hold on broad rollout of the new kernel selection until memory and tail-latency regressions resolved.
- Approve pre-warm buffer feature for Dedicated as an opt-in per-customer config.
- Add a new cross-team epi to reduce cold-start latency for quantized endpoints (Noor owner).

Action items (owner - due):
- Miguel: add KV cache and quantization telemetry to canary (due 2026-05-20)
- Sam: cost simulation for pre-warm buffer and proposal for toggles (due 2026-05-22)
- Noor: implement small warm cache prototype for quantized endpoints (due 2026-05-25)
- Evan: propose trace labeling convention for token-level cost attribution (due 2026-05-21)
- Ravi: freeze non-critical changes for 1.12 and finalize release checklist (freeze 2026-05-20, release 2026-05-25)
- Asha: review PD postmortem draft and customer communications (due 2026-05-19)

Risks / Blockers:
- Cost impact of pre-warm buffers could be non-trivial for high-commitment Dedicated customers - finance review required before GA.
- Long-context quantized path memory edge cases remain a blocker for full rollout of 8-bit optimizations for some models.
- Test infra flakes on multi-GPU CI slowing down release testing; Ravi to escalate if no improvement this week.

Follow-ups / Notes:
- We need a short-lived cross-team spike (2 weeks) to evaluate kernel selection machine-learning approach vs rules-based heuristics - Miguel to propose scope.
- Product requested a short customer-facing one-pager explaining Dedicated autoscaling behavior and what customers can configure; Hannah to draft.

Next meeting (weekly): 2026-05-25
Proposed agenda: canary soak update, pre-warm cost decision, release status and any blockers for 1.12, incident action review.

Attachments / links: see linked_artifacts above for PRs, Jira tickets and confluence roadmap.
